title: Retrospective study to evaluate the recurrence rate depending on the surgical procedure in patients with tenosynovial giant cell tumour (pigmented villonodular synovitis).The clinical parameters, such as the course and extent of the disease, the therapy and any local recurrence or progression of the disease are recorded.
summary:
Tenosynovial giant-cell tumor, historically known as pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS) is a benign but aggressive synovial proliferative lesion, first described by Chassaignac [1]. Later Jaffe et al. coined the term PVNS [2]. PVNS is a rare condition with an annual incidence of about 1.8 patients/million and with a peak in the third or fourth decade of life [3]. The knee joint is the most commonly affected joint, followed by the hip and ankle joints [4]. In tenosynovial tissue as seen in joints, tendon sheaths or bursae a proliferation of synoviocytes attracts inflammatory cells such as histiocytes and hemosiderin-laden macrophages [5].
The etiology of the lesion is still unknown but neoplastic clones found in PVNS often express colony-stimulating factor 1 (CSF1) and frequently have a t(1;2) translocation [6]. Either in a localized (nodular) or a diffuse type, brownish, villous and nodular growth is seen, sometimes invading the adjacent bone [7]. Malignant transformation is reported in very few cases [8]. Clinical presentation is nonspecific with symptoms as swelling, pain and joint locking by nodular lesions [9].
The mainstay of therapy is the surgical resection either with marginal excision in localized disease or with total synovectomy in diffusely involved joints or tendon sheaths. There is still controversy whether this should be done by aggressive open synovectomy or by an arthroscopic approach, if feasible [10,11]. Conventional radiotherapy as well as radiosynoviorthesis might also affect the rate of local recurrence or even cure the disease [12]. In recent years, systemic antibody treatment with PLX3397, a selective CSF1R inhibitor has shown some favorable results [5].
The aim of our study was to evaluate the main patients characteristics, treatment and outcomes in a large single-centre retrospective study, focusing on meticulous aggressive open surgical procedures.

interventions.name: The clinical symptoms of the patients are evaluated according to the course of the file, as well as local imaging (MRI) at the same intervals as during the clinical check-ups.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients with a tenosynovial giant cell tumour who undergo surgery at the study centre during the study period will be included.
Exclusion criteria:
None
